manuscript_findings.earlier_phase: The author's unfinished v4 manuscript: information literacy, educational misinformation/neuromyths, confidence versus competence, six framework traditions and an eight-pillar synthesis including metacognition and ethics/law.
manuscript_findings.later_phase: The author's unfinished v5.1 manuscript: deliberate disinformation, propaganda, information-psychological warfare, reflexive control, plausible deniability, algorithmic amplification, authoritarian populism, democratic fragility and human agency.
manuscript_findings.additional_influences: Propaganda analysis, misinformation persistence/correction, cognitive threat appraisal, human empowerment, and practical traceability/approval/recovery experience in the author's supplied CV.

corrections.subject: Tarasenko's book
corrections.finding: The supplied PDF's title/copyright pages and foreword identify Applications of the Reflexive Game Theory: Advanced Topics, 2016. The acknowledgments/preface describe nearly five years of collaboration with Lefebvre, not evidence of a formal five-year degree supervision.

corrections.subject: Tarasenko's article
corrections.finding: Emotionally Colorful Reflexive Games, submitted in 2010; the arXiv identifier begins 1101. The previously suggested 2017 article date is not used.

corrections.subject: 2025 internship
corrections.finding: The unfinished work was the author's separate ethical AI model, not the internship. A connection to neuromorphic work is suspected but unestablished.

corrections.subject: Theorem authorship
corrections.finding: The author attributes the originating experimental discoveries to his 2024 implementation; full formalization followed supplying Astra the entire historical code archive and collaborating on that material.

corrections.subject: Awareness and relationships
corrections.finding: Only Alan Cohen knew the current project existed. None of the acknowledged researchers saw, reviewed or approved the current model. Cohen was a personal friend/mentor, not a professional collaborator; Tarasenko's contact was limited to sharing PDFs.
